title: Calibration pipeline and nightly cosine-sim drift detector for embedding quant profiles
creator: Aisha Kline
description: Problem: We need an automated, low-noise pipeline to produce INT8 and FP16 quantization profiles for our embedding models and to continuously detect accuracy regressions using cosine similarity drift checks. Current manual calibration runs produce noisy baselines and truncation of SLO alerts, causing both missed regressions and alert fatigue. This ticket delivers a calibration pipeline plus a nightly drift detector that compares quantized outputs against our FP16 reference and triggers gated investigation workflows when similarity drops are statistically significant.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Nightly job runs without manual intervention and emits a summary artifact to S3 and the console dashboard. 2) Calibration produces an 'active' quant profile and a 'canary' profile; canary is tested on a holdout dataset and metrics recorded. 3) Drift detector computes per-corpus cosine deltas vs FP16 baseline and raises an alert if the 95th-percentile drop is greater than 0.02 or if median drops > 0.03 for two consecutive nights. 4) Playbook links appear in the alert and sample vectors are attached for quick triage. 5) PRs implementing the pipeline are merged and e2e tests pass in CI.
design_notes: We treat FP16 outputs as the reference distribution for similarity. For each quant profile (INT8/FP16 serving profile pair) the pipeline will: 1) sample a stratified corpus across major customer domains, 2) run deterministic embedding generation for N=10k anchors + 1k holdouts, 3) compute cosine similarity between quantized and FP16 vectors, and 4) summarize statistics including median, 5th/95th percentiles, and per-bucket means by sequence length and token distribution. We choose 95th-percentile guardrails to reduce sensitivity to long tails that occur during tokenization boundary cases. The pipeline stores per-anchor hash to allow stable comparisons on subsequent runs.
calibration_steps: - Stage 1: Offline calibration harness in GH action that executes quantization sweep across candidate scale factors and per-channel qparams. - Stage 2: Run int8 calibration for small set of layers with 'layerwise fallback' config to allow selective fp16 for sensitive layers. - Stage 3: Generate candidate quant profiles and produce canary artifacts in S3 under s3://redwood-quant/profiles/{model}/{date}/. - Stage 4: Canary evaluate against holdout and push results to metrics store and dashboard. - Stage 5: If canary passes thresholds, mark active and notify runtime config service to consider rollout.
monitoring_plan: Nightly cron job in scheduler service triggers a kubernetes job that pulls the latest active quant profile and runs the standardized evaluation harness. The job writes metrics to Datadog and emits an alert via PagerDuty when thresholds breached. Alert payload contains: model name, profile id, median similarity delta, 95th percentile delta, sample anchor IDs, and link to 'quantation-run' artifact in Confluence. We also persist a rolling 14-day window to compute trend slopes and reduce single-night flakiness.
thresholds: Guardrails: 95th-percentile cosine drop > 0.02 triggers P0 investigation. Secondary gate: median cosine drop > 0.03 across any corpus for 2 consecutive nights triggers automatic rollback of scheduled rollout and creates ENG rollback ticket. We also monitor embedding-based downstream recall degradation: if downstream nearest-neighbor recall@100 drops by > 1.5%, escalate to oncall and block releases.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Sensitivity vs noise: Choosing percentile-based thresholds reduces false positives but may miss gradual degradations; mitigated by trend slope checks over 14 days. - Compute cost: full nightly run across 10k anchors is expensive; mitigate with stratified sampling and incremental evaluation using cache deltas. - False positives from tokenizer drift or dataset shifts: include tokenization-version metadata and compare only anchors with matching tokenizer hashes. - Rollback risk: automatic rollback requires safety net approvals to avoid regression churn; initial rollout will use manual confirmation before automatic actions.
rollback_plan: If threshold breach is confirmed, steps: 1) Pause any canary/rollout in Console. 2) Revert runtime profile to last known-good profile via runtime-2.3 config endpoint. 3) Create ENG-RB-{date} ticket with attached artifacts and sampled vectors. 4) Run focused diagnostic: layer sensitivity scan and nearest-neighbor recall test. 5) If fix is low-risk (scale param tweak), publish patch and re-run canary.
